checks.claim: C1: C_sep and the raw objects k_f, U_q, H_(b,q), lambda_(b,q), I_psi and v_psi match the accepted lower theorem, and no covariance or kinetic convention is changed.
checks.reason: Target lines 9-17 match actual-shifted-event Sections 1-2 and the spectral note: same f,q class, k, U=Gamma*q, H_b=-d2-bU, and I_psi as the time integral of the ground rate. v_psi=E W(psi)^2 equals the integral of f(t)k_f(t) times <q,U_q> by tilt (5),(8). The amplitude and the white/Riesz endpoints are retained, and b=k_f(t) lies in the positive compact K_par of note (5).

checks.claim: C1: I_psi and v_psi are representation-independent, and the dilation is an intrinsic bijection of C_sep.
checks.reason: For nonzero nonnegative factors, f q=f' q' forces f'=l f and q'=q/l with l>0. Hence h_psi=k_f U_q is unchanged, so H at each t, its ground rate, I_psi and v_psi depend only on psi. psi_s(t,x)=s^(3-alpha)psi(t,sx) preserves the class because f is unchanged and q_s stays smooth, compact, nonnegative and nonzero. By hand, (psi_s)_r=psi_(rs), so the inverse is scale 1/s.

checks.claim: C2: q_s, the pushforward factor and U_(q_s)=s^2 U_q(sx) are exact at both Riesz and white endpoints.
checks.reason: Gamma(sA)=s^(1-alpha)Gamma(A) holds directly for c|x|^-alpha dx and for c delta_0. The pushforward under y->sy is Gamma(A/s)=s^(alpha-1)Gamma(A). So Gamma*q_s(x)=s^(3-alpha)s^(alpha-1)U_q(sx)=s^2U_q(sx). At alpha=1 this is c s^2 q(sx), with the true amplitude retained. No Fourier density or compact Riesz potential is used.

checks.claim: C2: the L2 unitary, H2 domain, s^2 energy scaling and s rate scaling are correct.
checks.reason: With (D_s g)(x)=sqrt(s)g(sx), hand recomputation gives H_(b,q_s)=s^2 D_s H_(b,q) D_s^-1, and D_s preserves H2. Thus E1 scales by s^2, simplicity and positivity of the ground state transfer, and lambda=sqrt(-E1) scales by s at the same b. Since k_f is unchanged, I_(psi_s)=s I_psi.

checks.claim: C2: raw variance scales by s^(4-alpha), not its square root; fixed-s use is legal without uniform estimates.
checks.reason: v_(psi_s)=A_f<q_s,U_(q_s)> with exponent (3-alpha)+2-1=4-alpha, where A_f is the double time integral of f against |t-u|^-a. Each fixed s gives a fixed member of C_sep, to which the accepted fixed-test theorem applies with its own K_par and constants. Target lines 19-21 and 67-68 exclude moving tests, s=s(delta) and uniform event claims.

checks.claim: C3: V_c is a well-defined positive finite real for every c>0, without an optimizer.
checks.reason: C_sep is nonempty. I_psi is positive and finite by note (6). v_psi is positive and finite because a<1, U_q is bounded, and all factors are nonnegative and nonzero. Each score at c=2 is at most Q2, and Q2 is at most the limsup, which is finite from E:full-upper because kappa>0 and the prefactor log is o(t^kappa). This bound is one number and is not a uniform event estimate. V_1>0 follows from s I-s^(4-alpha)v/2>0 for small s, since 4-alpha>1. All other c transfer by the dilation bijection.

checks.claim: C3: V_c=c^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha))V_1, V_2>2V_1 and Q2>=V_2 are correct and noncircular.
checks.reason: With c=s^(3-alpha), the score satisfies c I_(psi_s)-v_(psi_s)/2=s^(4-alpha)(I_psi-v_psi/2) exactly. Because the map is bijective, the suprema transform with no optimizer. The exponent lies in [4/3,3/2], so 2^p>2, and strictness uses 0<V_1<infinity. Q2>=V_2 is a supremum of fixed lower bounds on one fixed number, with no limit interchange. The upper input is an independent import that does not use V_c. Added falsification: inserting a covariance amplitude A gives V_c proportional to A^(1/(3-alpha)), matching the R_alpha^(1/(3-alpha)) power in T:full-upper.
